messages:
priya: Heads up — I want to follow up on the continuous batching RFC with a focused thread about fallback + shaping heuristics and a small API contract so runtimes can signal graceful degradation.
alex: Nice. quick summary of the gap? what are we missing from the current RFC?
priya: Current RFC defines admission, coalesce windows, and eviction but leaves fallback behavior underspecified. when a batcher decides it can't meet latency SLO it should be able to degrade gracefully (smaller batches, bypass cache, route to hot path) and signal that decision to upper layers for observability and routing. no standard field today.
mike-sre: +1. we also need to ensure fallbacks don't create feedback loops across tenants — one tenant forcing hot-path could cascade.
yana: Agree. proposal idea: runtime emits a small structured hint on responses when fallback happened, e.g. `fallback_reason: "latency_deadline"`, `fallback_type: "bypass_batch"`, `fallback_level: "soft|hard"` — optional field only for observability.
jamie: sounds good. does that mean changing public API shapes? need backward compat plan.
priya: Keep it additive and optional. Add a new top-level response header `x-rd-fallback` (JSON string) for hosted API, and an SDK-exposed property for private/dedicated. No change to core generation payload.
alex: how do we avoid perf overhead? serializing tiny header is cheap, but SDKs will need to avoid blocking paths.
mike-sre: agree; header build should be on fast path but only when a fallback flag flips. otherwise absent.
yana: on heuristics: propose two-level approach:
```
1) local fast heuristic: if queueing_delay + estimated_inflight > deadline_margin => bypass batch
2) aggregated safety: per-GPU token-rate limiter to prevent one tenant from forcing repeated bypasses
```
local heuristic runs per-admission path, aggregated safety enforced by admission controller.
jamie: Tradeoffs: local heuristic is low-latency but noisy. aggregated safety reduces noise but adds complexity + config.
priya: Telemetry: emit a counter `fallback.count{reason, type, tenant}` and a histogram `fallback.latency_impact` capturing delta vs expected latency.
alex: Also add a gauge `fallback.active` to detect persistent degradation.
mike-sre: Alerting: new alert when fallback.count spikes 5x baseline for 5m with top tenants listing.
yana: For rollout: start with internal canary for 2 weeks on non-critical regions, collect data, then 1% traffic experiment, then full rollout. Feature flag gated.
priya: Open question: should we offer a user-configurable policy: e.g. application may opt-out of bypass and accept higher latency for batch cost savings.
jamie: I think yes — customers should be able to prefer cost vs latency. add `fallback_policy: prefer_cost|prefer_latency|auto` in model route config.
alex: Implementation note: admission API needs a new callback `should_fallback(context) -> (bool, reason)` so custom schedulers can override heuristics.
mike-sre: We should also add a safe default that matches current behavior when policy not set.
priya: I'll draft RFC follow-up with config snippet + metrics + rollout plan. Owner: @priya. I'll open PR next week and tag runtime + infra owners.
deploy-bot: release-checklist: ensure header serialization unit tests, SDK opt-in flag, telemetry dashboards created.
priya: Thanks all. If no objections I'll post a short design doc and checklist by EOD tomorrow. :shipit:
